quiz.title: Unit 2 SAQ 03
quiz.headline: Indian Ocean exchange
quiz.prompt: Answer all parts of the question. Use evidence from the period c. 1200 to c. 1450.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Describe ONE way environmental knowledge shaped trade in the Indian Ocean.
criteria: Describes its effect on how trade was carried out.

model.answer: Knowledge of the monsoon winds set the schedule of Indian Ocean trade.
model.prove: Because the winds blow from the southwest in summer and from the northeast in winter, ships sailed out on one monsoon and returned on the other.
model.explain: Sailors who understood the pattern could plan predictable round trips, which made regular long-distance trade possible.

parts.alternatives: Navigational knowledge of stars and coastlines, used with the astrolabe and compass, can also work.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way merchant diasporas affected Indian Ocean port cities.
criteria: Names a specific diaspora community or port.
Explains a cultural, social, or economic effect on the city.

model.answer: Merchant diasporas brought Islam and new customs into port cities.
model.prove: Arab and Persian merchants settled in Swahili cities such as Kilwa and married into local families, and Swahili developed as a Bantu language with many Arabic loanwords.
model.explain: Because merchants stayed for months or settled permanently while waiting for the winds, cultural exchange became part of everyday life in the ports rather than a brief contact.

parts.alternatives: Chinese merchant communities in Southeast Asia, or Muslim communities in Calicut and Quanzhou that built mosques and appointed judges, can also work.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way a state used Indian Ocean trade to increase its power.
criteria: Explains how trade added to that state's revenue, prestige, or control.

model.answer: Malacca used its control of a strategic strait to become a powerful sultanate.
model.prove: In the 1400s Malacca's rulers taxed ships passing between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea and used naval forces to protect traffic.
model.explain: Customs revenue from a passage that ships could not easily avoid paid for the navy and court that made Malacca a regional power.

parts.alternatives: Swahili city-states taxing trade in gold and ivory, or the Ming using Zheng He's voyages to gain tribute and prestige, can also work.
